### Discovery & Translational Science

* **Safety hazard identified for ortho-carborane mixtures** [Science](https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/safety-warning-carborane-mixtures)
  * A new publication in *Inorganic Chemistry* warns that ortho-carborane—a boron-rich cage cluster widely explored in medicinal chemistry and boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT)—poses a significant, previously unrecognized explosion hazard when mixed with a variety of common laboratory materials.
  * Ortho-carboranes are prized in oncology drug discovery for their high boron-10 (¹⁰B) neutron cross-section, which captures low-energy neutrons to emit high-energy α-particles that destroy localized tumor tissue.

* **Large-scale genomic analysis identifies novel risk genes for neurodegenerative diseases** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.03.26347540)
  * A population-scale gene-burden testing analysis of rare damaging coding variants identified *IMPA2* as a novel risk gene associated with Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD).
  * The study also uncovered novel Parkinson's disease and related disorders (PDRD) associations at *ANKRD27* and *CCL7*, with the strongest signal at *ANKRD27* clustering within domains that mediate interactions with Rab GTPases and retromer components.

* **Rare human MYCBP2 variant enhances memory persistence across species** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.1101/2024.12.18.24319147)
  * Whole-exome sequencing of an individual with highly superior autobiographical memory (HSAM) identified a rare, de novo *MYCBP2* V768F missense variant affecting an evolutionarily conserved residue in the encoded E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase.
  * In vivo engineering of the homologous substitution in *C. elegans* and heterozygous knock-in mice improved long-term memory retention without affecting baseline sensory, motor, or growth phenotypes.
  * Selective prime editing of the variant in the dorsal hippocampal neurons of adult mice was sufficient to enhance spatial long-term memory, demonstrating that its cognitive effects do not require developmental expression.

* **Single-cell profiling reveals placental alterations in PMOS non-responsive to metformin** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.21.26353338)
  * Multimodal single-cell molecular analysis of placentas from pregnancies with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) revealed cell-type-specific transcriptional downregulation and altered cell-type proportions.
  * Syncytiotrophoblasts exhibited reduced growth hormone receptor signaling activity, while endothelial cells showed diminished receptor tyrosine kinase pathway activity (including VEGFC) despite increased hypervascularity.
  * Metformin treatment induced minimal molecular improvements in PMOS placentas, with its associated transcriptional shifts linked to lower birth weight and higher childhood BMI.

* **Calmodulin mutation N54I drives CPVT in a novel heterozygous mouse model** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.09.12.751164)
  * A heterozygous mouse model carrying the human disease-associated *Calm1* N54I mutation showed that mutant calmodulin, which accounted for just 13.7% of total cardiac calmodulin, is sufficient to drive arrhythmogenic phenotypes.
  * Isolated cardiomyocytes showed increased rates of RyR2-mediated spontaneous calcium release, while conscious mutant mice exhibited significant ventricular ectopy, ventricular tachycardia, and atrial electrical abnormalities under catecholaminergic or exercise challenges.

* **ACNP outlines collaborative roadmap for psychiatric precision biomarkers** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760290/)
  * The American College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ACNP) issued a position paper outlining a collaborative roadmap designed to establish actionable biomarkers for precision clinical trials in psychiatry.

* **Expression of Concern issued for EZH2 study in SWI/SNF-mutant cancers** [Nature Medicine](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41591-026-04708-9)
  * *Nature Medicine* has published an Editorial Expression of Concern regarding a paper examining the dependence of SWI/SNF-mutant cancers on the catalytic and non-catalytic activity of EZH2.

* **Other Discovery & Translational Highlights**
  * A systematic review of early-life serum protein profiles identified biomarkers associated with bronchopulmonary dysplasia in extremely preterm infants [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760543/).
  * A study on endocrine regulation in mice shows that a high-salt diet modulates the feedback loop between cortisol and FGF23 [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760427/).
  * A review highlights the re-emergence of covalent modulation as a key therapeutic modality in modern drug discovery [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760582/).
  * Researchers developed a high-throughput evidence-generation workflow using linked EHR and claims data to run comparative-effectiveness evaluations across complex comorbid populations [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.07.26350300).

### Early Trials — Phase I–II

* **Esketamine evaluated for postoperative pulmonary complications in lung cancer surgery** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760676/)
  * A randomized, double-blind, controlled trial evaluated the efficacy of esketamine on postoperative pulmonary complications in patients undergoing radical surgery for lung cancer.

### Late & Pivotal Trials — Phase III

* **[Biotech]** **Xenon pauses enrollment in Phase 3 depression trials of azetukalner** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/xenon-azetukalner-depression-trial-halt-adverse-events/830756/)
  * Xenon Pharmaceuticals paused enrollment in its Phase 3 trials evaluating lead candidate azetukalner in depression following the emergence of "neuropsychiatric adverse events."
  * The adverse events were described as mild-to-moderate, short-lived, and reversible, and are consistent with the drug's potassium channel-opening mechanism of action. The trials will continue with already-enrolled patients and expect data in early 2027.
  * Azetukalner is currently under FDA review for a seizure disorder (epilepsy), and analysts suggest the psychiatric events in the depression cohort are unlikely to impact the regulatory path in epilepsy.

* **Randomized controlled trial of video game therapeutic Meliora shows no increase in gaming-related problems** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.03.04.26347656)
  * A three-arm randomized controlled trial of 1,001 adults with major depressive disorder (MDD) evaluated the long-term adjunctive use of the video game therapeutic Meliora.
  * Over 12 weeks, Game Addiction Scale (GAS-7) scores decreased significantly in the Meliora group (mean change, -0.63 points), showing a greater reduction compared to a sham video game control (mean change, -0.02; p = 0.001) and similar outcomes to treatment-as-usual (TAU).
  * The results suggest that long-term use of this digital therapeutic does not promote gaming addiction or related behavioral issues.

### Regulatory & Approvals

* **[Big Pharma]** **FDA approves Lilly’s Inluriyo in combination with Verzenio for ESR1-mutated metastatic breast cancer** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/resources-information-approved-drugs/fda-approves-imlunestrant-combination-abemaciclib-er-positive-her2-negative-esr1-mutated-advanced-or)
  * The FDA approved Eli Lilly's oral selective estrogen receptor degrader (SERD) imlunestrant (Inluriyo) in combination with abemaciclib (Verzenio) for adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated advanced or metastatic breast cancer.
  * The approval is supported by the Phase 3 EMBER-3 trial, which enrolled 874 patients with disease progression following at least one line of endocrine therapy.
  * The Guardant360 CDx assay was simultaneously approved as a companion diagnostic to identify patients with ESR1 mutations.

* **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Ultragenyx’s gene therapy Fayuvi for Sanfilippo syndrome Type A** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/ultragenyx-fayuvi-orum-bristol-lunsumio-longeveron-rocket-danon/830512/)
  * The FDA approved Ultragenyx's Fayuvi, the first gene therapy for the rare, progressive neurodegenerative condition Sanfilippo syndrome Type A.
  * Fayuvi has been priced at $3.95 million. Alongside the approval, Ultragenyx received a valuable priority review voucher to bolster its balance sheet.

* **[Biotech]** **FDA approves Scholar Rock's apitegromab as first therapy for muscle loss in SMA** [PubMed](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42760382/) / [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * The FDA has approved Scholar Rock's apitegromab, the first myostatin-targeted monoclonal antibody approved to treat muscle loss in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA).

* **[Biotech]** **CHMP recommends EU approval for Corcept’s Lifyorli in hypercortisolism** [Corcept / X (formerly Twitter)](https://x.com/BioStocks/status/2100918962879856949)
  * The EMA's Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) has recommended marketing authorization for Corcept Therapeutics' Lifyorli (relacorilant).

* **FDA approves Aqneursa for ataxia in patients with ataxia-telangiectasia** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/fda-approves-therapy-treat-ataxia-patients-ataxia-telangiectasia-rare-genetic-disorder)
  * The FDA approved Aqneursa (levacetylleucine) for oral suspension to treat ataxia in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg with ataxia-telangiectasia.
  * Aqneursa is the first approved treatment for ataxia in this rare genetic neurodegenerative population. The efficacy was demonstrated in a 73-patient, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial (NCT06673056).

* **Additional FDA Approvals and Regulatory Actions** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/news-events-human-drugs/whats-new-related-drugs)
  * **Kybella labeling update**: The FDA approved a labeling update for Kybella (deoxycholic acid) injection to include warnings about adverse reactions associated with unapproved uses.
  * **Joenja (leniolisib) pediatric expansion**: Pharming Group's leniolisib received approval for the treatment of APDS (activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome) in pediatric patients aged 4 to 11 years (approved Sept 9, 2026).
  * **Camizestrant accelerated approval**: The FDA granted accelerated approval to AstraZeneca's camizestrant in combination with a CDK4/6 inhibitor for ESR1-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer (approved Sept 4, 2026).
  * **Sevabertinib accelerated approval**: The FDA granted accelerated approval to Bayer's kinase inhibitor sevabertinib (Hyrnuo) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic non-squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring HER2 tyrosine kinase domain (TKD) activating mutations.

* **FDA accelerates adoption of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) to replace animal testing** [FDA](http://www.fda.gov/drugs/science-and-research-drugs/cder-streamlined-nonclinical-studies-and-acceptable-new-approach-methodologies-nams)
  * The FDA issued a Year One progress report on its roadmap to reduce, refine, and replace animal testing with human-relevant methods, such as organs-on-chips, AI-powered models, and in silico tools.
  * The agency launched a public NAMs database featuring real-world examples of alternative methods accepted in approved drug applications, and announced it will begin accepting sponsor applications for Year 5 of its Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls (CMC) Development and Readiness Pilot (CDRP) on October 1, 2026.

### Business & Strategy

* **[Big Pharma]** **GSK aggressively builds oncology pipeline through China licensing deals** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/biotech-charts-gsk-china-electra-ipo-scholar-rock/830514/)
  * GSK has secured five licensing deals with Chinese drug developers since early 2025, trailing only Roche in sourcing clinical assets from China.
  * Recent transactions include a partnership with Hutchmed for an antibody-targeted therapy conjugate, and an alliance with Chimagen Biosciences for a trispecific myeloma candidate.
  * GSK's 2023 partnership with Hansoh Pharma yielded a lung cancer therapeutic that recently delivered promising data at the World Conference on Lung Cancer.

* **[Biotech]** **Marea Therapeutics secures backdoor listing via Lisata Therapeutics acquisition** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/lisata-marea-deal-acquire-cardiovascular-endocrine-disease-drugs/830717/)
  * Marea Therapeutics has entered public markets through an acquisition by Lisata Therapeutics. Marea stockholders will own ~60% of the combined entity, with Lisata shareholders holding just over 2%.
  * A prominent investor syndicate (including Forbion, venBio, and Third Rock Ventures) has committed $225 million in concurrent financing to support the clinical pipeline.
  * The transaction centers on MAR001/005, an ANGPTL4 inhibitor licensed from Novartis in Phase 2b for severe hypertriglyceridemia, and MAR002, a Phase 2 candidate for acromegaly.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Bristol Myers Squibb terminates Orum AML collaboration after Phase 1 readout** [BioPharma Dive](https://www.biopharmadive.com/news/ultragenyx-fayuvi-orum-bristol-lunsumio-longeveron-rocket-danon/830512/)
  * BMS has returned the rights to ORM-6151, an experimental acute myeloid leukemia (AML) therapy licensed from Orum Therapeutics in 2023 for $100 million upfront.
  * The program—which combined antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) and targeted protein degradation (TPD) technologies—was discontinued following a review of Phase 1 clinical data. Orum will forfeit up to $80 million in potential milestone payments.

* **[Big Pharma]** **Roche expands Boston footprint with new research center** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/18/biotech-news-roche-expands-it-boston-footprint-with-research-center/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * Roche is establishing a new research center in Boston, expanding its early-stage R&D presence in the major biotech hub.

* **U.S. draft investment rules expected to preserve China licensing deals** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/pharmalot/2026/09/18/rules-for-china-licensing-deals-making-drugs-in-space/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * New U.S. treasury rules governing investments in China are expected to carve out and preserve the pharmaceutical industry's ability to execute standard in-licensing deals for Chinese-developed therapeutics.

### Public Health & Policy

* **White House touts "GENEROUS" Medicaid drug discount program** [STAT+](https://www.statnews.com/2026/09/18/trump-touts-state-participation-generous-medicaid-drug-discount-program/?utm_campaign=rss)
  * The Trump administration announced that all 50 states will participate in the new GENEROUS program, aimed at securing deep discounts on prescription medications for state Medicaid programs. Exact operational details and pricing structures remain undisclosed.

* **Proportional naloxone scale-up yields highly variable county-level overdose mortality reductions** [Research Preprint](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.05.11.26352900)
  * A simulation model calibrated across six Pennsylvania counties projected that a uniform 30% increase in naloxone distribution would yield highly heterogenous public health benefits by 2029.
  * The model projected a 70% reduction in overdose deaths in urban Allegheny County, but only an 11% reduction in intermediate-sized Erie County and a 28% reduction in rural Clearfield County.
  * Conversely, increasing buprenorphine dispensing by 30% yielded a larger benefit than naloxone in Erie County (20% vs. 11% reduction), highlighting that local resource allocation should be tailored to historical dispensing patterns rather than uniform federal or state targets.

**Worth watching:** How the regulatory review of Xenon's azetukalner in epilepsy is impacted by the newly reported mild-to-moderate, reversible neuropsychiatric adverse events that triggered a pause in its Phase 3 depression program.
